capitals.name: Malayu (Jambi, on the Batang Hari)
capitals.note: The page places the kingdom around the Batang Hari in 'Jambi and West Sumatra' and names no site or date for the early seat; Jambi city is the researcher's pin for it.

capitals.name: Dharmasraya (Padang Roco, upper Batang Hari)
capitals.note: First dated Dharmasraya: the Padang Roco inscription of 1286 placing the Amoghapasa statue 'at Dharmasraya'; the infobox lists 'Minanga Dharmasraya Pagaruyung' without dates and the page gives no date for any relocation from Jambi.

rulers.name: Trailokyaraja
rulers.note: Named in the Grahi inscription of 1183 (infobox: Trailokyaraja, 1183); the only year the page gives.

rulers.name: Tribhuwanaraja
rulers.note: Infobox 1286-1316; the Pamalayu page calls him 'their king, Tribhuwanaraja'.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). The page gives 'Earliest mention: 671' (Yijing) and places the kingdom in Jambi; no extent, so a 100 km disc on Jambi. Infobox area: none given.

Dharmasraya, the upper Batang Hari (Padang Roco)

correction.text: Malayu-Jambi on the lower Batang Hari and Dharmasraya on its upper course, where the 1286 inscription stands

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page says independence was restored in 1028 and that Jambi led the 'Sanfoqi' missions from the 11th century; the later seat is Dharmasraya (1286). Extent is the researcher's two-disc reading, soft. The page is silent on borders, and Jambi 'became independent' only in the early 13th century on the Srivijaya page (srivijaya dossier, loss 1202); the 1288-1293 Javanese occupation is carried by the singhasari dossier's vassal span 1290-1292. fx-32 (F201): the 1028 start is kept (Srivijaya page: 'after 1025 the term Sanfoqi referred to the Malayu Dharmasraya kingdom where the mandala was re-centred'); srivijaya no longer draws this outline from 1028.

region.text: Malayu on the Batang Hari around Jambi

ledger.note: 671: the kingdom of Malayu is first named, by the monk Yijing. 'Earliest mention: 671'; 'In 7th century, the first use of the term for a nation or a kingdom was recorded by Yijing.' The page gives a first mention, not a founding.

692: Srivijaya absorbs Melayu. Infobox 'Annexed by Srivijaya: 692'; 'absorbed by Srivijaya by 692'; Yijing wrote that Malayu changed its name to Sribogha (the srivijaya dossier carries the matching merge).

union.text: Malayu on the Batang Hari around Jambi
Dharmasraya, the upper Batang Hari (Padang Roco)

ledger.note: 1028: Melayu-Jambi stands apart from Palembang again. Key date 'Independence restored' (1028); the 1028 'Sanfoqi' mission 'would actually refer to Malayu-Jambi, not Srivijaya-Palembang'; from the 11th century Jambi takes the leadership of Sanfoqi. The Srivijaya page (srivijaya dossier, loss 1202) puts Jambi's independence in the early 13th century: the two pages disagree and the reviewer should read both. fx-32 (F201): srivijaya's keyframes and a 1028 loss now agree with this date; its 1202 loss covers only the rest of the Jambi province.

1286: Dharmasraya is the seat. The Padang Roco inscription dated 1286 'states that a religious statue of Amoghapasa was established at Dharmasraya', and the page reads 'bhumi Malayu' there as Dharmasraya; no page dates the move from Jambi, so the year is the first dated mention (page silent on the move).

region.text: Melayu / Malayapura, passing to Adityawarman's kingdom

ledger.note: 1347: Adityawarman takes Melayu from the Majapahit queen and makes it his own. 'Adityawarman was made ruler of Melayu by the Majapahit queen. He later founded a kingdom in Pagaruyung'; the Amoghapasa inscription is dated 1347 and names Malayapura (Pagaruyung page: 'in 1347 Adityawarman proclaimed himself king in Malayapura'). Infobox successors: Pagaruyung Kingdom, Majapahit Empire and the Kingdom of Singapura (no territory on the page for Singapura).

wars.name: Pamalayu expedition

zones.text: Jambi (Malayu), conquered 1288 on the Melayu page
Palembang, conquered by Mahesa Anabrang in 1288

wars.outcome: 'The expedition arguably established Javanese domination over Melayu and trade in the Strait of Malacca'; Mahesa Anabrang 'conquered Palembang and Jambi (Malayu)' in 1288, an alliance by marriage with two Malay princesses sent to Java, and the force 'returned to Java on 3 May 1293'.
wars.note: Decreed in 1275 'though perhaps not undertaken until later'; the Amoghapasa statue of 1286 stands at Dharmasraya under King Tribhuwanaraja. The vassal span is carried by the singhasari dossier (1290-1292), the Palembang occupation by the srivijaya dossier (1288-1293).

wars.name: Malayu invasion of Java (Anjukladang inscription)
wars.outcome: The Anjukladang inscription of 937 'refers to repelling invading forces from Malayu'; no territorial result.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer sees it was considered: Melayu is 'absorbed' by Srivijaya in 692 on the same page, so the invaders are Srivijaya-era Malay forces.

certainty.note: Inscriptions and Chinese reports name the kingdom and its seat but no frontier; every outline is a disc on a river valley.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for Melayu (its 'Malaya' 1294-1351 is the Malay Peninsula). Wikidata id not looked up (wikidata.org unreachable): null. The page is thin on territory: every outline is the researcher's disc on the Jambi lowlands and the upper Batang Hari. No page dates the move from Jambi to Dharmasraya. The srivijaya dossier carries the 692 merge and a 1202 loss of Jambi; this dossier takes 1028 from the Melayu page's own date list, so 1028-1201 is a disagreement between the two. The Majapahit dossier carries Jambi-Melayu as a vassal sphere from 1352; Adityawarman's own kingdom (1347) is the pagaruyung-kingdom dossier. The infobox lists Srivijaya as predecessor; predecessors is left empty because Srivijaya's own start (671) is the same year as Melayu's first mention. The Kingdom of Singapura listed among the successors has no territory on this page. Gazetteer: Dharmasraya and Padang Roco (upper Batang Hari, about 1.1 S 101.6 E), Muara Jambi are not in places.jsonl. | fx-32 F201: date settled at 1028 for the Melayu core (this dossier's L2); srivijaya now subtracts the Melayu outline from its keyframes 1028-1293 and carries the matching loss in 1028, with the rest of the Jambi province lost in 1202.
